items.title: Section: A King Immune to Both False Blame and False Praise

items.zh: 復次，如佛世尊為出愛王所說經言：彼王一時往詣佛所，頂禮佛足，白言：世尊！有一沙門、若婆羅門來至我所，以不真實過失，現前呵諫於我，我於爾時，其心不生悔惱憂慼。何以故？觀此過失，於我自身都不見故。又有沙門、若婆羅門來至我所，以不真實功德，現前讚勸於我，我於爾時，心亦不生歡喜踊躍。何以故？觀此功德，於我自身都不見故。
items.en: Moreover, as the Blessed One taught in the sutra spoken for King Udayana: that king once went to where the Buddha was, bowed at the Buddha's feet, and said: Blessed One, when some ascetic or brahmin comes before me and rebukes me to my face with an untrue fault, my mind at that time feels no regret, distress, or sorrow. Why is this so? Because, examining this fault, I find no trace of it in myself. And when some ascetic or brahmin comes before me and praises me to my face with an untrue virtue, my mind at that time likewise feels no joy or elation. Why is this so? Because, examining this virtue, I find no trace of it in myself either.

items.zh: 彼諸沙門及婆羅門既退還已，我便獨處空閑靜室，生如是心籌量尋伺：我當云何了知諸王真實過失、真實功德？若我知者，當捨其失，當修其德。誰有沙門、或婆羅門，能了諸王真實過失、真實功德，亦能為我廣開示者？既尋伺已，便作是念：唯我世尊一切知者、一切見者，定當了知諸王所有真實過失、真實功德，我今當往佛世尊所，請問斯義。故我今者來至佛所，請決是義，唯願如來為我開示。世尊！云何諸王真實過失？云何諸王真實功德？作是請已。

items.title: Section: The Buddha Names Ten Faults of a King

items.zh: 爾時，世尊告出愛王曰：大王！大王今者應當了知王之過失、王之功德、王衰損門、王方便門、王可愛法，及能引發王可愛法。云何名為王之過失？大王當知！王過失者略有十種。王若成就如是過失，雖有大府庫、有大輔佐、有大軍眾，然不可歸仰。何等為十？一、種姓不高，二、不得自在，三、立性暴惡，四、猛利憤發，五、恩惠奢薄，六、受邪佞言，七、所作不思不順儀則，八、不顧善法，九、不知差別忘所作恩，十、一向縱任專行放逸。
items.en: At that time, the Blessed One told King Udayana: Great King, you should now know a king's own faults, a king's own virtues, the gateways of a king's own decline, the skilful means of a king, the qualities beloved of a king, and what draws forth those beloved qualities. What is called a king's own fault? Great King, you should know that a king's faults are, in brief, of ten kinds. If a king possesses such faults, though he has a great treasury, great ministers, and a great army, he does not deserve reliance. What are the ten? First, low birth. Second, lack of sovereign authority. Third, a naturally cruel disposition. Fourth, fierce, uncontrolled anger. Fifth, sparing and stingy kindness. Sixth, heeding deceitful counsel. Seventh, acting without thought and without regard for proper protocol. Eighth, disregarding wholesome dharma. Ninth, failing to distinguish and forgetting kindness received. Tenth, wholly indulgent and heedless conduct.

items.title: Section: Five Shades of Royal Cruelty, and the Gravest of Them All

items.zh: 云何名王種姓不高？謂有國王，隨一下類王家而生，非宿尊貴；或雖於此王家而生，賤女之子，不相似子；或是大臣、輔相、國師、群官等子。如是名王種姓不高。云何名王不得自在？謂有國王，為諸大臣、輔相、國師、群官所制，不隨所欲作所應作，錫賚群臣；於妙五欲，亦不如意歡娛遊戲。如是名王不得自在。云何名王立性暴惡？謂有國王，諸群臣類或餘人等，隨於一處現行少小不如意事，即便對面擯黜，發麁惡言，咆勃忿恚，顰蹙而住，時生憤發。設不對面，背彼向餘而作於前擯辱等事。設不對面、亦不背彼向餘而作於前黜罵等事，然唯內意憤恚欝怏，懷惱害心，懷怨恨心，然不長時持憤恚心相續不捨。復有內意憤恚欝怏，懷惱害心、懷怨恨心，亦於長時持憤恚心相續不捨。由如是相對面暴惡、背面暴惡、懊恚暴惡、暫時暴惡、長久暴惡，如是名王立性暴惡。大王當知！長久暴惡名獲大罪，非是餘者。
items.en: What is called a king's low birth? A king born into some inferior royal house, not one of long-standing eminence; or, though born within such a house, the child of a lowly woman, not resembling the true heir; or the child of a minister, chancellor, royal preceptor, or official. This is called a king's low birth. What is called a king's lack of sovereign authority? A king controlled by his own ministers, chancellors, preceptors, and officials, unable to act and reward according to his own wish, nor freely enjoy the finest pleasures. This is called lack of sovereign authority. A king whose ministers or others, wherever some slight displeasure arises, are immediately banished to his face, met with coarse language, furious shouting, and a scowling countenance, erupting in anger. Or, not to their face, doing the same behind their back before others. Or, neither to their face nor behind their back, yet inwardly harbouring resentment and malice, though not sustained for long. Or further, inwardly harbouring resentment and malice, sustained over a long time without release. Great King, you should know that it is specifically this long-sustained cruelty that constitutes a grave fault, not the others.

blocks.text: Fascicle 61 explains a sūtra in which a king asks the Buddha what the true faults and true virtues of a ruler are. It is the treatise's most practical teaching on leadership.

subs.head: Unmoved by false blame or praise

blocks.text: The king's calm rests on self-examination: the fault is simply not found in him. Master Cháng Bǎi: a practitioner is the same; slandered for a fault one lacks, there is no need to mind; praised for a virtue one lacks, no need to be glad.

The king tells the Buddha that after the ascetics and brahmins left, he reflected alone: "How can I know the true faults and true virtues of a king, so as to give up the one and cultivate the other? Only the Blessed One, who knows and sees all, can tell me." So he has come to ask.

Faults, virtues, gates of decline, gates of skilful means, what a king wants, and what brings it: these six outline the whole sūtra. Master Cháng Bǎi: though a faulty king has a full treasury, good ministers, and a strong army, one should not rely on him.

Master Cháng Bǎi: a king without real authority is controlled by his ministers and cannot reward or punish rightly. Of the kinds of cruelty, long-lasting cruelty is the gravest; one who flares up and soon calms is less harmful.
The king's first virtue is not power but self-knowledge: false blame cannot touch someone who has looked honestly at themselves.

quiz.q: King Udayana says that an untrue fault rebuked to his face causes him no distress. Why?
options: because, examining the fault, he finds no trace of it in himself
because a king outranks ascetics and need not heed any rebuke at all
because he has attained an unshakable mind that no blame can move
because he believes the ascetic has some hidden motive for rebuking
quiz.why: The king's calm rests on self-examination, not on rank or attainment. The fault is simply not found in him, and the same reasoning applies to untrue praise. Master Cháng Bǎi repeats that the fault cannot be found in him.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi apply the king's words to practitioners?
options: every slander should be accepted and confessed, since others see one more clearly than one does oneself
one should avoid all criticism
a slander of a fault one lacks need not trouble one, nor praise of a virtue one lacks delight one
one should seek out others' praise
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a practitioner is the same; if slandered for a fault one lacks, there is no need to mind, and if praised for a virtue one lacks, no need to be glad. The measure stays with what is actually found in oneself.

quiz.q: What six things does the Blessed One tell the king to know?
options: faults, virtues, treasury, ministers, army, and the beloved qualities
ten good deeds, five precepts, giving, morality, meditation, wisdom
faults, virtues, gateways of decline, skilful means, beloved qualities, and what draws those qualities forth
lineage, mastery, cruelty, anger, kindness, and heedlessness
quiz.why: The six are the outline of the whole sutra. Treasury, ministers, and army appear in the next sentence as outward assets that do not save a faulty king; they are not among the six. Lineage through heedlessness belong within the ten faults.

quiz.q: With the ten faults, a king still has a great treasury, ministers, and army. How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the conclusion?
options: as long as treasury and army are strong one may still rely on him until he reforms
ministers may no longer advise him
neighbouring states will surely attack
even with riches, able ministers, and a strong army, one should not go to this king for refuge or rely on him
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: though such a king has a full treasury, good ministers, and a strong army, one should not go to him for refuge. Whether he deserves reliance depends on character, not resources, as §6 confirms from the other side.

quiz.q: §2 renders 王方便門 as "the skilful means of a king." What is missing compared with its neighbours?
options: 門: the same sentence has "gateways of decline," so the paired sets no longer match
方便: the term means a city gate and has nothing to do with skill, as the lecture plainly states
it omits 王
nothing, §11 having the same wording
quiz.why: The treatise pairs 衰損門 and 方便門, and §11 and §17 both use "gateway." Only §2 drops it, so the English hides the pairing of five gates of decline with five gates of skilful means that Master Cháng Bǎi lists together.

quiz.q: Which of these is not part of a king's low birth as the treatise describes it?
options: being born into an inferior royal house, not of long-standing eminence
being born into an eminent house and resembling the true heir
being the child of a lowly woman, though born within such a house
being the child of a minister, chancellor, preceptor, or official
quiz.why: The treatise gives three cases: an inferior house, the child of a lowly woman, and the child of an official. Option A is the opposite, noble lineage, defined in §6. Master Cháng Bǎi glosses 非宿尊貴 as lacking a long noble tradition.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain 相似子, the heir who resembles?
options: anyone who looks like the king, whatever his birth, so even a commoner may qualify
a son adopted by the king
the most trusted of the ministers
the son of the queen consort, given the best upbringing, alike in form to the king
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a child of a lowly woman will not much resemble the king; only a true heir born of the queen consort, given the best upbringing from childhood and alike in form, is called the resembling child. §6 then uses this term.

quiz.q: What is meant by a king's 不得自在?
options: he cannot restrain his own temper and erupts at every displeasure, which the text next calls long cruelty
he is controlled by his ministers and cannot reward or act as he wishes, nor enjoy the pleasures freely
he is too ill to govern
he has been conquered by a neighbour
quiz.why: The term concerns royal power, not emotional control. Master Cháng Bǎi: he is controlled by ministers, preceptors, and officials, and cannot do what he should or reward his officials as he wishes. Temper is treated separately as cruelty.

quiz.q: The English heading for 不得自在 is "lack of self-mastery." Why does it mislead?
options: it does not mislead, since 自在 means restraining oneself, and the English definition agrees
it reads as poor self-control, whereas the text means royal power checked by ministers
自在 should be "freedom from death"
"lack" should be "absence"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi explains the term as being controlled by ministers. The English definition in §3 is right, but the label "self-mastery" suggests self-restraint and overlaps with the tenth item on heedlessness. A term such as "sovereign autonomy" would fit.

quiz.q: Which cruelty does the treatise say constitutes a grave fault?
options: the long-sustained cruelty that holds on to resentment without release
the open cruelty that banishes and curses to one's face, since all can see it
a brief inward anger soon let go
cruelty voiced behind their backs
quiz.why: The treatise singles out duration, not visibility. Master Cháng Bǎi: long-lasting cruelty is the king's greatest fault; the other kinds are not yet so great. One who flares up and soon lets go, he adds, does not keep thinking of it.
